name: Pixelsort
author: E. T. Carter
description: A pixel-sorted photograph: a soft landscape of lit sky, low sun, drifting cloud and dark treeline, scanned row by row so every run brighter than a threshold is smeared into a monotone gradient that ends in a hard edge. Run edges break into ragged teeth as the threshold jitters per row, and the streaks grow, snap and re-form as the clouds drift and the threshold breathes.

params.label: Threshold
params.effect: Brightness above which a run is sorted; low smears most of the picture into streaks, high touches only the sun and cloud rims.

params.label: Tooth
params.effect: Per-row threshold jitter; 0 gives smooth run edges, 1 the fully ragged sawtooth of a real sort.

params.label: Direction
params.effect: 0 sorts along rows so the streaks run horizontally, 1 sorts down columns.

params.label: Picture scale
params.effect: Feature scale of the picture underneath; low is a few broad cloud masses, high is a busy sky that breaks into many short runs.

params.label: Drift
params.effect: How fast the clouds drift and the threshold breathes; 0 freezes the sort.

params.label: Mouse influence
params.effect: How far the pointer dips the sort threshold around it; 0 ignores the mouse.
